figures.caption: Fig. 1: A conceptual comparison between traditional hashing frameworks and our proposed TriPAH framework.

Fig. 2: The overall framework of TriPAH. It consists of four main components: (I) Semantic Context Adaptive Prompting, where patient-level prompts p̃i are synthesized via stochastic gating to complement raw reports; (II) Feature Extraction, utilizing CLIP encoders with visual prompt injection; (III) Tri-view Semantic Fusion, employing Mamba-Transformer blocks for pairwise interaction among image text and prompt; and (IV) Imbalance-aware Multi-task Hashing, where binary codes are optimized via asymmetric quantization and class-balanced supervision Lcbce to handle long-tailed medical distributions.

TABLE I: Performance comparison (mAP ↑) of different cross-modal hashing methods on ODIR-5K [19], MIMIC-CXR [2], and IU-Xray [20] datasets. The best results are highlighted in bold, and the second-best results are underlined.

Fig. 3: Qualitative visualization of cross-modal retrieval results on heterogeneous medical datasets. (Top) On the ODIR-5K dataset (fundus images), TriPAH accurately retrieves reports matching specific diagnostic keywords like “normal fundus” and “retinopathy” based on visual cues. (Bottom) On the IU-Xray dataset (chest X-rays).
